summary: Frontend-only regression test of the RadarView.tsx pinch/pan Follow-Mode fix (pinchActive shared value + Pan.requireExternalGestureToFail(pinch)). Tested via browser Preview (mobile viewport 375x667) using kauri@intro.demo (token injected via localStorage; visibility toggled to true via PUT /api/users/me/state since account defaulted to invisible on load, matching prior iteration's note). Zoom buttons (+/-, x4 each direction) and double-tap zoom-in/zoom-out were verified extensively: the 'You' marker's screen position never drifted by even 1px across any of these actions, and the locate/recentre icon stayed teal (rgb(32,178,170), Follow Mode ON) throughout -- this part of the fix is working correctly. However, a CRITICAL regression was found: a genuine single-finger drag/pan on the Radar never activates at all -- tried both via mouse down/move/up simulation AND via CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent (real single-touch touchStart/touchMove/touchEnd sequence) -- in both cases the map never panned, the 'You' marker never moved, and Follow Mode/locate button stayed teal instead of turning grey. This directly fails one of the explicitly-requested, browser-testable bullets ('single-finger pan MUST disable Follow Mode and let the map move freely'). Root cause is very likely `.requireExternalGestureToFail(pinch)` on the Pan gesture: Gesture.Pinch() defaults to requiring 2 pointers, so with only 1 finger down it never begins, and the gesture-handler web runtime does not appear to ever emit the 'pinch has failed' signal Pan is waiting on while only a single pointer is active (or only emits it too late, at pointer-up) -- so Pan can never leave its UNDETERMINED/waiting state during a live 1-finger touch, effectively deadlocking single-finger panning entirely in this Preview environment. Because pan never activates, the two dependent bullets (recentre-after-manual-pan, zoom-while-unfollowed-and-not-centred) could not be exercised either since Follow Mode never turns off manually. Rings/clusters/business+event markers/filters/radius chip/events chip all rendered correctly with no crashes or console errors across all tested states. Real 2-finger pinch simulation was not attempted (time-boxed after finding the pan blocker) -- per the task note, treat that specific bullet as an explicit known limitation of this session, not a false pass/fail.

integration_issues.issue: Pan gesture never activates/never fires onStart-onUpdate-onEnd during a live single-finger drag, reproduced with both mouse-event simulation and CDP-dispatched real single-touch events. Follow Mode stays ON (locate button stays teal) and the map/'You' marker never move, even mid-drag while the finger/pointer is still down and after release. Likely caused by `.requireExternalGestureToFail(pinch)` on the Pan gesture never resolving (Pinch requires 2 pointers and never begins with 1 finger, so it appears to never signal FAILED in time for Pan to activate) -- effectively deadlocking manual panning.

verified_working: Radar tab loads with no crash/red-screen/console errors after the fix
'You' marker screen position identical (pixel-exact, 188,315 baseline) across: zoom-in x4, zoom-out x4, double-tap zoom-in, double-tap zoom-out -- zero drift in any state
Locate/recentre button colour stays teal rgb(32,178,170) (Follow Mode ON) throughout all zoom-button and double-tap actions -- never turns grey when only zooming
No regressions: rings, clusters, business/event pins, radius chip, filters chip, events chip, focus-summary chip all render correctly with no crash/console errors across every tested state
action_items: CRITICAL: Fix single-finger Pan so it can actually activate during a live 1-finger touch. Reproduced 100% in browser Preview with both mouse simulation and CDP real single-touch dispatch -- Follow Mode never turns off and the map never pans no matter how long/far the drag. Suspect `.requireExternalGestureToFail(pinch)` is the culprit (Pinch requires 2 pointers so it never reaches a FAILED state in time while only 1 finger is down). Consider removing requireExternalGestureToFail and relying solely on the pinchActive early-return double safety net (which was described as already sufficient per the task's own fix rationale), or use blocksExternalGesture/activeOffsetX-style tuning instead, or verify gesture-handler's web runtime actually emits the required FAILED signal for a still-live insufficient-pointer gesture.

Re-test after the pan fix: verify Follow Mode disables (grey) on real single-finger drag, recentre button restores teal + re-centres the map after a manual pan, and zoom +/- still works correctly while Follow Mode is off and the viewport is not centred (none of these 3 bullets could be exercised this session because pan never activated to put the app into the 'unfollowed' state).

Genuine 2-finger pinch simulation (CDP dispatchTouchEvent with 2 touchPoints) was not attempted this session -- recommend the next testing pass attempt it now that basic gesture arbitration needs a closer look anyway.
critical_code_review_comments: pinch.onStart/onUpdate/onEnd correctly only ever touches pinchActive/scale/tierSV/savedScale/tx/ty and never followSV/setFollowMode -- matches the described intent that pinching alone must never disable Follow Mode.
pan.onStart/onUpdate/onEnd all correctly early-return while pinchActive.value is true, which is the intended double-safety-net -- this part is sound in isolation.

The risk is specifically `.requireExternalGestureToFail(pinch)` combined with Pinch's default minPointers=2: on a platform/runtime where a not-yet-satisfied multi-pointer gesture doesn't promptly transition to FAILED while a single pointer is still down, this makes Pan wait indefinitely, i.e. it can never win the arbitration during an actual 1-finger touch. Given this reproduced identically with a real single-touch CDP dispatch (not just mouse emulation), this looks like a genuine cross-platform risk, not just a Playwright/browser-only artifact -- worth validating on a real device build too before considering this fix fully safe.

success_rate.frontend: 6/9 requested checks fully passed (zoom buttons x2 dirs, double-tap x2 dirs, no-drift, no-regression); 1 critical fail (single-finger pan never activates); 2 checks blocked/untestable as a direct consequence of the pan failure (recentre-after-pan, zoom-while-unfollowed); 1 explicit known limitation (2-finger pinch not simulated)

seed_data_creation: None new. Reused kauri@intro.demo (toggled visible=true via PUT /api/users/me/state, reversible/non-destructive, consistent with iteration_93's note that this account defaults to invisible on fresh login).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use kauri@intro.demo, token via localStorage auth_token (JSON-stringified) then reload, then PUT /api/users/me/state {visible:true} via API if the radar shows 'invisible' state (UI 'Turn Visibility On' button click did not work in Playwright -- had to call the API directly). A ping popup modal ('Someone nearby needs advice...') may appear over the Radar tab on load -- dismiss via the 'Dismiss' text button before interacting with the map. To check 'You' marker centring precisely, do NOT rely on `[data-testid=radar-recentre]` alone for colour -- read `div[style*='ionicons']` inside it and check `.style.color` (teal = rgb(32,178,170)). To locate the 'You' text label precisely (it's not the marker centre itself -- it sits ~38.5px below the true avatar centre by design, spacing is constant), filter all leaf DOM nodes with textContent === 'You' whose bounding-box Y falls within the radar-map's bounding rect (there are decoy 'You' nodes elsewhere on the page). Single-finger pan simulation via plain Playwright mouse.move/down/up did NOT trigger the gesture at all -- also tried CDP session.send('Input.dispatchTouchEvent', ...) with real touchStart/touchMove/touchEnd and got the identical null result, so this is very likely a genuine app-level gesture-arbitration bug, not a testing-tool limitation.
rca_of_issue: Symptom: single-finger drag/pan on the Radar view has zero effect -- Follow Mode never disables, map/marker never move -- reproduced identically with mouse-event simulation and real CDP single-touch dispatch, both mid-drag (while pointer still down) and after release. Likely cause: `Gesture.Pan().requireExternalGestureToFail(pinch)` where `pinch = Gesture.Pinch()` defaults to requiring 2 simultaneous pointers. With only 1 finger ever touching, Pinch cannot begin, and apparently does not promptly signal a FAILED state back to the gesture-handler runtime while that single pointer remains active (or does so only after all pointers lift, by which time Pan's own gesture window has also already closed) -- so Pan is stuck waiting for a failure signal from Pinch that never arrives in a usable timeframe, and it can never activate during an actual 1-finger interaction. Suggested mitigation to hand to the dev: drop `requireExternalGestureToFail(pinch)` entirely and rely on the pinchActive-based early-returns already present in Pan's onStart/onUpdate/onEnd (per the fix's own stated design, that double safety net was supposed to be sufficient on its own); if requireExternalGestureToFail is kept for a specific reason, it needs a real-device (not just Preview) verification pass plus possibly a timeout/blocksExternalGesture alternative since the browser Preview and CDP-simulated real touch both show the same deadlock.
